alex_sales: Hey team — Enterprise POC (Cardinal Health) wants a confirmed capacity plan for a 12-month reserved commit. Customer targets: 120 RPS steady-state, short spikes up to 300 RPS (5-min windows). Avg output ~60 tokens/request, model = quantized 13B with KV cache warmup. They asked: how many reserved GPUs, preheat plan, autoscale policy, and answers for security questionnaire (KMS/audit/data). Also need a ballpark committed pricing vs burst credits. Any blockers?

maria_solutions: Thanks — noted. Commit preferred = reserved pool + burst credits for spikes. Quick q: target p95 latency SLO?

alex_sales: p95 <= 300ms end-to-end for generation (network excluded). Customer will accept fallback to smaller model if we document expected quality tradeoff.

cheng_eng: Short calc for sizing: steady tokens/s = `120 * 60 = 7200 tps`. Peak tokens/s = `300 * 60 = 18,000 tps`. On our quantized 13B, one A100/80GB w/ optimized kernels + batching + warm KV ≈ 9k tps (estimate). So mapping: 9k tps per GPU -> steady = 1 GPU, peak ≈ 2 GPUs. Recommend: reserved pool = 2 GPUs, provide 2x burst credits to absorb short spikes, and autoscale policy up to 4 GPUs for safety during extended surges. Also recommend KV preheat (see below).

nina_sre: Preheat plan: rolling KV warmup job 10m before known traffic windows + on deploys. Warmup job should hit customer keyspace at low RPS to populate KV (e.g., 20 RPS for 5m). For Private deployments we need preheat ACL + RBAC entry for warmup runner.

kyle_billing: Pricing note (ballpark): 2 reserved A100 equiv GPUs ~ $XXk/mo (will send formal quote). Burst credits purchased as a pool; usage billed from pool at discounted rate. Private/on-prem has additional platform license fee. I'll attach numbers to the deal doc.

alex_sales: Security Qs from customer: do we support CMK (customer-managed keys), can we expose audit logs, and what's our default data persistence behavior?

nina_sre: Short answers: CMK yes (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) + HSM option for Private. Audit logs: available via Console/export to S3, retention configurable in contract. Data persistence: hosted default = no long-term request storage unless enabled; we can enable log export/retention per customer. SOC2/HIPAA support available — legal to add contract clauses.

cheng_eng: Autoscale policy suggestion (concrete): base = 2 reserved GPUs; scale-out trigger = avg GPU util > 75% for 60s OR request queue depth > 30; each scale = +1 GPU; cooldown = 10m; max = 4 GPUs. Fallback chain: if scaling unavailable, route to a 7B model variant automatically or reduce max_tokens/beam to preserve latency. We'll provide a config snippet for runtime.

alex_sales: Can we produce a short SLO vs quality doc showing latency/quality tradeoffs for fallback options for legal & customer?

maria_solutions: Yep — I’ll draft a 1-pager comparing 13B quantized vs 7B quantized vs policy degrade (reduce max_tokens by 30%).

ops-bot: playbook-bot: scheduled preheat job template created -> /playbooks/preheat/cardinal.yaml

alex_sales: Thanks — tagging @security_bot to review the KMS and audit note.

security_bot: ack — will review and add the required contract clauses for CMK/HSM and retention.

cheng_eng: Warmup snippet (example):
```
# warmup.sh
for i in {1..10}; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"warmup","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```

maria_solutions: I'll bundle the sizing calc, autoscale policy, preheat playbook, and security QAs into the PRD and ping legal + sales ops.

alex_sales: Action items: cheng to confirm exact per-GPU tps for our quantized build (cheng -> EOD), nina to prepare security questionnaire answers (nina -> EOD), kyle to produce formal pricing quote (kyle -> EOD), maria to prepare SLO-fallback 1-pager (maria -> EOD). We need to turn around by Monday for customer call.

alex_sales: Summary for customer reply I'll send tomorrow: reserve 2 GPUs (base), burst credits for short spikes, autoscale config up to 4 GPUs, KV preheat + warmup playbook, and security/KMS answers attached. No blockers identified. :thumbsup:
